title: Scope ACP `_omp/usage` to the requested session; record the stdio single-client attachment assumption at all seven unchecked `#sessions.get` sites
wave: Wave 2 — Correctness trên các đường đang ship (W4, W6, W12, W13)
one_line: `_omp/usage` currently answers with the FIRST session in the agent's map no matter which session the client asked about; make it resolve `params.sessionId`, and add comments (not guards) at the seven session lookups that carry no attachment check.
user_visible_effect: An ACP client asking for token/quota usage of session B today gets session A's numbers. After this change it gets B's. No new UI, no new flags, no default behavior change for any single-session client.
effort: S — one handler case (~+2/-1 lines) plus seven comment blocks and one test. Plan rates it S and that is accurate.
risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is ADDING FENCING — rejecting sessions without an attachment check — instead of writing the comment. The plan calls this out explicitly. The seven lookups are safe today only because the stdio transport carries exactly one client per connection; a fence there breaks the legitimate single-client path. Second-most-likely mistake: fixing the `unknown sessionId` case by falling back to `#initialSession`, which silently reproduces the very bug W4 removes (asking about session B and getting A's numbers back).

test_contract:
CONTRACT: `_omp/usage` reports the usage of the session named by `params.sessionId`, and no other session's. WHAT A CONSUMER OBSERVES IF IT REGRESSES: an ACP client with two live sessions renders the wrong quota/token panel — asking about session B and showing session A's numbers — with no error, no empty state, and nothing in the log to distinguish it from correct output. That is why the assertion must be on WHICH session's payload comes back, and must include the negative (`not.toContainEqual`) leg: with a single session the bug is invisible, so a test that only opens one session would pass against the broken code.

BOUNDARY ALSO COVERED BY THE SAME PRODUCTION CODE (assert it if cheap, otherwise leave it — do not build a second test around it): when `params.sessionId` names a session that is not in `#sessions`, the handler must return `{ reports: [] }` and must NOT return the initial session's or another session's reports. This is the negative half of the fix and is the case most likely to be 'fixed' wrongly by adding a `?? this.#initialSession` fallback.

WHAT NOT TO TEST: the comment half of this item. It documents a transport assumption and has no observable behavior. Per AGENTS.md, a test that asserts on comment text is a banned source-grep, and a test that asserts 'the code ran' is a placeholder.

plan_corrections.correction: `_omp/usage` has ZERO callers anywhere in this repository (`git grep -rn '_omp/usage'` returns only the server-side case label at :1180), so it is consumed by an EXTERNAL client this repo cannot see. The existing `?? this.#initialSession` fallback is therefore load-bearing for any client that calls without a sessionId, and the fix must preserve it. Two distinct branches are required and the spec makes the asymmetry explicit: absent sessionId keeps the old chain; present-but-unknown sessionId resolves to nothing. Collapsing both into one expression is where the bug gets half-fixed.

open_questions: Should a supplied-but-unknown `sessionId` return `{ reports: [] }` (this spec's recommendation — non-breaking, no other session's numbers) or throw an ACP error (matching `#getSessionRecord`'s strictness)? This is a wire-visible choice for an external client we cannot see in this repo. The spec picks `[]` because the handler already has that branch and throwing turns a data gap into a client error. A human should confirm before merge; changing it later is a one-line edit either way.

Should all seven sites carry the full rationale block, or one full block at `#getSessionRecord` (:1384) plus a two-line cross-reference at the other six (this spec's recommendation)? The plan says 'đặt comment tại cả bảy điểm', which a strict reading makes a seven-fold duplicated paragraph. The spec's split still records the assumption at every site, which is the point, without the drift risk of seven copies. Deviation is deliberate — flag it in the PR description.

Is there a reason `_omp/usage` should not accept a sessionId at all (i.e. should the client instead be expected to call a per-session method)? No in-repo caller exists to arbitrate this, and the fix direction is the smaller change, so the spec proceeds with it.
